subject: Request: Custom availability credit and latency guardrail approval for Nebula Analytics
messages:
From: Sofia Rami <sofia.rami@nebula.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@nebula.ai>
Date: 2027-03-25T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: availability target + latency carveout for initial onboarding

Hi Irene / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Nebula is excited about building with Redwood. We have two asks tied to our procurement timeline:

1) During our initial 6-month migration window we need an availability target of 99.95% (versus your standard 99.99%) for our US + APAC workloads due to expected cross-region cold-cache churn.
2) We need a latency guardrail: a P95 target of 350ms for the same period, and we want a structured approach to credits only if we miss both availability and latency concurrently.

Procurement is asking for an explicit cap on monthly service credits (we'd expect credits to be limited so our auditors can sign off). We are also price-sensitive during onboarding and will prioritize vendors that offer limited credit exposure plus a modest onboarding credit.

Can you confirm if Redwood is willing to consider a temporary SLO variance and a capped credit structure? Our ideal timeline is to have terms agreed by 2027-04-05 to hit our procurement window.

Thanks,
Sofia Rami
Head of Cloud Platform
Nebula Analytics

Attachments: initial-architecture-diagram.png (image stub)

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Rami <sofia.rami@nebula.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-26T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: availability target + latency carveout for initial onboarding

Sofia —

Appreciate the clear ask and timeline. We can evaluate a temporary SLO variance but need to align commercial guardrails and engineering mitigations before committing. High-level thoughts:

- Availability: provisional target 99.95% for first 6 months is plausible, subject to an aggregate annual credit cap.
- Credits: rather than open-ended monthly credits, propose a monthly cap at X% (TBD) and a 12-month aggregate cap; we typically prefer an aggregate cap to avoid runaway exposure.
- Latency: we can include a P95 latency target of 350ms but recommend credits only trigger when both availability and latency are missed in the same billing period (reduces double-dipping).

I will run impact numbers and route to Deal Desk / Finance for a commercial cap recommendation. Rishi, can your team confirm whether the engineering mitigations (autoscaling, cache pre-warm hooks) are reasonable to target for the onboarding window?

Irene
Irene Choi
Manager, Deal Desk
Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: Nebula SLO request — exec approval needed

Marissa / Jonas — forwarding Nebula's ask. Key commercial asks combined with procurement timeline:

- Temporary availability target 99.95% for first 6 months across US+APAC
- P95 latency target 350ms during same period; credits only if both availability and latency missed in a billing month
- Customer requests a clear monthly credit cap so their auditors can sign off; Nebula indicated they'd favor a modest onboarding credit in exchange for tighter cap.

Deal metrics: ARR ~ $450k first year; expansion potential substantial. Concession ask: limit cumulative credit exposure to no more than 8% of monthly invoice (customer wants clarity). They are also asking for a one-time onboarding credit; Ben suggests we offer up to $30k onboarding credit if we get a 12-month commit and a 10% introductory discount.

Irene and Rishi have started an impact analysis (see attached nebula_slo-impact-analysis.pdf). We need exec authorization for (a) availability variance, (b) an aggregate credit cap, and (c) whether to include the one-time onboarding credit.

Short timeline: customer wants contracts signed by 2027-04-05.

Ben
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: nebula_slo-impact-analysis.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Legal <legal@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-01T14:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Nebula SLO request — exec approval needed

Team — thanks for the summary and for the impact analysis. I am willing to approve a constrained, temporary deviation with the following conditions:

1) Availability: authorize 99.95% for the initial 6-month onboarding period for US + APAC only.
2) Credits: cap monthly service credits at 4% of that month's invoice; additionally, add an annual aggregate cap of 8% of total invoices in a 12-month rolling window. No cumulative credits beyond that aggregate cap.
3) Latency: include P95 350ms as a paired metric but only trigger credits when both availability and latency are missed in the same month.
4) Commercial offsets: authorize a one-time onboarding credit up to $25,000 provided Nebula signs a 12-month committed term and agrees to a joint 90-day technical review cadence with our CS/Infra teams.
5) Risk controls: require Legal to add a clause that: (a) prevents credit stacking across multiple SLOs, (b) permits Redwood to suspend the special terms if traffic patterns indicate misuse, and (c) mandates an engineering remediation plan within 30 days of first breach.

These concessions should be documented as an MSA exhibit and scoped to a discrete onboarding window — do not bake into the long-term MSA. I will sign-off on these conditions; Legal and Jonas please produce the final MSA excerpt and run the financial impact to ensure profitability.

Marissa Cole
VP, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-slo-terms-v2.docx, slo-cost-analysis.xlsx

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Rami <sofia.rami@nebula.ai>, Procurement <procurement@nebula.ai>

Date: 2027-04-02T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Approved: Nebula onboarding SLO variance and commercial terms (next steps)

Sofia —

Thanks for your patience. Per internal approvals, Redwood can offer the following to support Nebula's onboarding:

- Temporary availability target: 99.95% for the first 6 months (US + APAC only).
- Service credit structure: monthly credit capped at 4% of that month's invoice; 12-month aggregate cap at 8% of total invoices.
- Latency: P95 target 350ms; credits only if both availability and latency are missed in the same billing month.
- One-time onboarding credit: $25,000 applied to the first invoice if Nebula executes a 12-month committed term and agrees to the 90-day joint review cadence.

Deliverables / next steps:
1) Legal will email an MSA exhibit (attached: nebula-msa-excerpt.pdf) reflecting the clauses Marissa requested (no credit stacking, suspension right, remediation timeline).
2) Finance will reflect the one-time credit in the quote and confirm expected margin impacts (Jonas).
3) Engineering (Rishi) will schedule a remediation/mitigation plan and pre-warm playbook before go-live.
4) I will send a DocuSign link for the MSA exhibit once Legal finalizes wording: https://app.redwood.com/docusign/nebula-8812

Sofia, can you confirm you can sign by 2027-04-05? If so, we'll lock the onboarding credit and apply the commitments above.

Best,
Irene Choi

Redwood Inference
